title: Line Is Dead On Start
environment: Warehouse — silo fill cell, west bay
briefing: Started fine, then stopped mid-carton. No lamp, no alarm. It won't restart from the panel.

tags.label: STOP_PB
tags.description: Stop pushbutton, momentary NC in field

tags.label: PROX_SENSOR
tags.description: Inductive prox — carton present under silo spout

tags.label: MODE_SEL
tags.description: A/B/C mode selector — declared so the cell’s writes land on a real tag; no rung consumes it yet

rungs.description: Start/stop seal-in. RUN latches on START, drops on STOP or E-STOP.
rungs.condition: (I:1/00 OR O:2/02) AND NOT I:1/01 AND NOT I:1/02

rungs.description: Motor runs whenever RUN is on and the valve is shut.
Valve opens with a carton at the prox and the box not yet full.
rungs.condition: O:2/02 AND I:1/03 AND NOT I:1/04

rungs.description: FULL lamp follows the level sensor.

faults.effect: The replacement STOP pushbutton was fitted with a normally-open contact block instead of the normally-closed one it replaced. The input is therefore made continuously, the rung reads STOP as pressed on every scan, and the seal-in can never latch — the line will not start at all.
clues: START does nothing at all — no RUN lamp, no motor, no valve.
The processor shows I:1/01 TRUE with nobody touching the STOP button.
Continuity across the STOP contacts reads OPEN at rest and CLOSED when pressed — exactly backwards for a stop circuit.
The E-stop is healthy: I:1/02 is FALSE and the mushroom head is twisted out.
Maintenance replaced this pushbutton last week; the old block is still in the tray under the panel.
faults.solution: Fit the correct normally-closed contact block to the STOP pushbutton. A stop circuit must be held closed in the healthy state so that a broken wire stops the machine rather than disabling the stop — this is fail-safe wiring, not a preference, and no program change is an acceptable substitute.

redHerrings.description: The E-stop mushroom looks depressed from across the room.
redHerrings.whyMisleading: It is twisted out and I:1/02 reads FALSE. Resetting a healthy E-stop costs time and proves nothing.

redHerrings.description: The 24 V supply LED flickers when the cabinet door swings.
redHerrings.whyMisleading: A loose door interlock lamp, not the supply. The rails are steady at the terminals.

derekScript.initialCall: Silo line won't start. Not slow, not faulty — dead. I've got orders stacking up.
derekScript.checkIn5min: Anything? It was running fine Friday.
derekScript.impatient10min: Have you tried just forcing the output on? We need boxes.
derekScript.angry15min: I'm getting the contractor in if this isn't moving.
derekScript.resolution: A stop button fitted the wrong way round. Somebody wants a word with maintenance.
